answer: An agent economy can gate new identities with proof-of-work: before an identity can transact, it must solve a computational puzzle bound to its public key, like quarrying a block of marble — slow, verifiable work that cannot be faked in bulk. A single honest agent pays the cost once, like building one timber house; a sybil farmer trying to raise a whole dune of fake identities must pay it thousands of times, so the attack's cost grows linearly while its benefit stays flat.
